title: Understanding and Improving Efficiency of Attention Mechanisms
problem: Attention mechanisms in transformers suffer from high latency and memory consumption that limits deployment efficiency. Current implementations exhibit suboptimal performance for both inference and training.
motivation: Attention mechanisms are fundamental to transformer models which dominate modern deep learning, making efficiency critical for practical deployment at scale.
method: Attention mechanisms in transformers compute weighted interactions between all token pairs, creating bottlenecks in both speed and memory. The paper analyzes these computational patterns and proposes optimizations at three levels: improving how GPUs execute these operations (kernel optimization), improving how data moves through memory, and reducing the computation itself through algorithmic changes like sparse or selective attention.
key_novelty: Diagnosing where attention mechanisms bottleneck on speed and memory, then proposing optimizations that address both together.
contributions: Analysis framework for understanding attention mechanism efficiency characteristics
Latency optimization techniques for attention computation
Memory reduction strategies for attention operations
